title: RiceDroid 8.6 GSI on Xiaomi 11T Pro Install Android 13 Guide

video_description:
RiceDroid 8.6 as a GSI on the Xiaomi 11T Pro — Android 13 installed over the vendor image, with the exact fastboot commands and the wipe step people always forget.

This build is a generic system image, phh-treble based, so the ROM itself is clean and the device side of things depends entirely on your vendor and kernel. That's the whole trade: you can put it on almost anything Treble, but how well the camera or calls behave is your vendor's business, not the ROM's.

📱 Device  : Xiaomi 11T Pro
🧩 ROM     : RiceDroid 8.6 (GSI, phh-treble)
🤖 Android : 13
👤 Credits : @LynixFox

🛠️ What You Need
• Unlocked bootloader and a Treble-ready device
• The RiceDroid 8.6 system image — ARM64 or A64 AB, GApps, vanilla and slim builds are all available
• The vbmeta file and platform tools on your PC
• A working custom recovery for the final data wipe

📝 Steps
1. fastboot reboot fastboot
2. fastboot --disable-verity --disable-verification flash vbmeta
3. fastboot erase system
4. fastboot flash system
5. fastboot reboot recovery
6. Wipe data in Mi Recovery
7. Reboot. Done.

⚠️ Where People Get Stuck
• Skipping the vbmeta flags. Without disabling verity and verification, the GSI won't boot.
• Forgetting the data wipe at the end. A dirty system partition plus old userdata is the classic bootloop.
• Blaming the ROM for broken hardware features. On a GSI, camera, calls and sensors ride on your vendor and kernel, and the ROM can't fix that.

Known bugs: nothing listed in the ROM itself, which is rare and nice. On the device side, it really does depend on your vendor and kernel. SELinux works both ways here — enforcing and permissive are both fine.
